title: AI and Machine Learning Fundamentals
objective: Explain the roles of AI, machine learning, and generative AI, as well as the workflow from training through inference to monitoring.

sections.title: Choose a Method Based on the Objective
paragraphs: AI is a broad concept that supports or automates intellectual work. Machine learning is a method that learns patterns from data, while generative AI is an application that generates text, images, and other content. Start by considering the required outcome—such as prediction, classification, or generation—and choose explicit rules for tasks that must always produce the same result under fixed conditions.

sections.title: Distinguishing Learning Methods by Correct Labels and Rewards
paragraphs: Supervised learning classifies and predicts unknown inputs from inputs and correct labels. Unsupervised learning finds groups of similar features without correct labels. Reinforcement learning learns a policy from rewards received as a result of actions. For every method, verify that the data represents actual usage conditions.

sections.title: Choose based on the requirements: data type, inference mode, and delivery method
paragraphs: The choice of preprocessing and services changes depending on whether the data is tabular or consists of text, images, audio, or video. Consider real-time inference when a response is needed during the interaction, batch inference when you want to process a large amount of input together, and asynchronous inference when you accept input and return the result later. In a screen that generates text, displaying the response as each portion becomes available is called streaming. With Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker AI, you can entrust part of the operations to AWS, depending on the service. If you host the model yourself, you are also responsible for updating and monitoring the runtime environment.

You can use Amazon Transcribe to transcribe speech, Amazon Translate to translate text, and Amazon Comprehend to extract entities from text. Amazon Lex is available for conversational bots, and Amazon Polly is available for text-to-speech. Choose the service based on the required inputs and outputs.

checkpoints.prompt: A retail company's analyst wants to use the labels "fraudulent" and "not fraudulent" attached to past orders to classify new orders into those two categories. Choose the one most appropriate learning method.

choices.explanation: It learns to classify from inputs and their correct labels.
It finds patterns without correct labels.
It learns from the rewards resulting from its actions.

checkpoints.prompt: The operations manager at a logistics company has started using a shipment-volume forecasting model in production. To determine whether forecast accuracy has declined during the busy season, select the one most appropriate method.

choices.text: Stop monitoring after the initial evaluation.
Observe the actual inputs and results, and evaluate declines in accuracy and changes in the data.
choices.explanation: This supports decisions about reevaluation and retraining.

choices.text: Automatically retrain the model every time and omit evaluation.
choices.explanation: The effects of retraining cannot be verified.

checkpoints.prompt: An HR department staff member is designing a process that approves only applications that exactly match fixed conditions. Which implementation should be chosen first?

choices.text: Have generative AI generate the approval decision.
choices.explanation: Its outputs can vary, making it unsuitable for strict condition evaluation.
This does not execute fixed conditions.

choices.text: Evaluate the conditions using explicit business rules.
choices.explanation: Rule-based methods are appropriate for business processes whose outcomes are uniquely determined.
